study.title: Microsite availability, not floral herbivory, limits recruitment in peripheral native thistle populations
published_conclusions: Reducing head insect herbivory increases lifetime estimated viable seeds
Greater seeds do not yield a proportional increase in local seedling recruitment
Elevation changes flowering phenology but not herbivory effect in this study

published_numeric_positive_control.source: Russell et al. 2025 Ecosphere DOI 10.1002/ecs2.70310 Table 4
published_numeric_positive_control.unit: estimated viable seeds per whole mother plant; original published means (SE)
published_numeric_positive_control.2018_intervention_artifact: Tanglefoot accidentally destroyed early buds; author applies head-position-aware replacement-seed estimates
published_numeric_positive_control.recruitment_result: No significant treatment gain in recruitment; 26/210 maternal plants produced no local seedlings despite 24 of these 26 producing viable seed
published_numeric_positive_control.pollen_interpretation: Original authors found no evidence insecticide impaired pollination; comparison on undamaged heads is not independent pollen-deposition assay.

independent_life_stage_context_studies.approach: Concurrent contrasts of predispersal insect predation, postdispersal vertebrate predation and grass competition
supported_observations: About threefold decline in viable seeds with insect feeding accompanied by approximately sixfold decline in seedlings
Sixfold to 37-fold fewer eventual new adults in original experimental comparisons
Strong postdispersal context dependence including grass competition

independent_life_stage_context_studies.habitat: Arapaho Prairie Preserve and Niobrara Valley Preserve, Nebraska Sandhills
independent_life_stage_context_studies.approach: Four levels of seed addition with seedlings and reproductive adults followed for 9 years
supported_observations: Strong seed limitation of seedling and adult recruitment at both sites
Relative importance of seed limitation declines with plant age
Postdispersal density dependence differs between the two sites

independent_life_stage_context_studies.habitat: Five Colorado montane grassland sites at western xeric range periphery
independent_life_stage_context_studies.approach: Plant-randomized flower head insect-herbivory reduction in 2017–2019, seed output and 2-year recruits within 2 m of mother
supported_observations: Viable maternal seed output increased with herbivore suppression
No proportional or statistically detected increase in nearby seedling recruitment under this treatment
Response may saturate with safe microsite availability in these source contexts

cross_context_conclusion.supported: Same Cirsium species can show strong seed-input limits to seedling/adult recruitment in some locations and a shallow local recruitment response to reduced herbivore seed loss in different locations/designs
not_supported: Proven change of genetic selection direction on spine or head angle
The 2020 and 2025 experiments estimate the same parameter
Universal absence of seed limitation at range margins
No plant fitness benefit because 2m seedling count unchanged
Effects pooled across 1990, 2020 and 2025 as independent equivalent replicates
cross_context_conclusion.scientific_priority: Distinguish genuine head architecture -> confirmed guild entry -> seed fate from context-dependent seed output -> recruited descendants
